intro.title: Simple Todo List
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Todo List application where you can add, view, and delete tasks. You will learn how to manage component state in React using the useState hook to store and update your list of todos. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and JSX for structuring the user interface. By the end, you'll have a working app that demonstrates fundamental React state management and event handling.
intro.usecase: Todo lists are foundational UI patterns found in countless real-world applications. You'll see similar implementations in project management tools like Trello or Asana for tracking tasks, in e-commerce sites for managing shopping carts or wishlists, and in productivity apps for daily checklists. As a developer, you'll frequently build interfaces that allow users to create, read, update, and delete items—whether it's managing user accounts in an admin dashboard, organizing content in a CMS, or handling items in any data-driven interface. Mastering this pattern gives you the core skills for building interactive data management features that appear across web and mobile applications.
